story: Ask HN: What's the best technical talk you've heard?
text: Andrew Tanenbaum presenting on Minix 3's architecture: [VIDEO] . Regardless of one's opinions on microkernels vs. monolithic kernels, it's a very interesting but accessible talk for those interested in lower-level systems and fault-tolerant architectures.
It's also for security. If you find a security vulnerability in e.g. the sound driver, you're not going to get root access. Andrew Tanenbaum explains it well: [VIDEO]

story: Hobby kernel and userspace, built mostly from scratch

story: Ask HN: Best practices for self-healing apps?
text: Here's you some examples to learn from. Most are old enough that patents have expired: Why Do Computers Stop and What Can Be Done About It? (1985) [LINK] Their NonStop Architecture [LINK] QNX's systems are ultra-reliable, too [LINK] OpenVMS clusters' uptime was years to decades & mixed CPU ISA's [LINK] Systems that run forever and self-heal (Armstrong) [LINK] Microreboots [LINK] Minix 3: Microkernel-based, self-healing, POSIX OS [VIDEO]
